question.value: How does infalling envelope gas connect to the Keplerian disk around the Class I protostar L1489 IRS, and what are the disk and infall properties?

evidence.quote: Our next interest is direct imaging of the transition from an outer infalling envelope to an inner Keplerian disk in protostellar sources.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00210.S.
The ALMA Band 6 observations of L1489 IRS were made with its extended configuration of 23 antennas at the cycle 0 stage on 2012 August 9.

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: FDM, 4 spectral windows of 234 MHz, 3840 channels each, Hanning smoothed, 122 kHz resolution (~0.17 km/s C18O/SO, ~0.16 km/s 12CO)

evidence.quote: The correlator was configured in the Frequency Division Mode (FDM) to provide four independent spectral windows with a bandwidth of 234 MHz.
Hanning smoothing was applied to the spectral channels, resulting in a frequency resolution of 122 kHz.

continuum_bandwidth.value: ~550 MHz at 225 GHz, from emission-free channels

evidence.quote: Emission-free channels in all of the four spectral windows were integrated to create the continuum image, which has a central frequency of 225 GHz and a bandwidth of $\sim$550 MHz.
The ALMA Band 6 observations of L1489 IRS were made with its extended configuration of 23 antennas at the cycle 0 stage on 2012 August 9.
The projected $uv$ distances range from $\sim$13 m to $\sim$383 m
The synthesized beams of the CLEANed images are 0.92$''$ $\times$ 0.71$''$ for the 1.3 mm continuum, 0.85$''$ $\times$ 0.72$''$ for the $^{12}$CO line
our observations are insensitive to structures at the scales larger than 17$\ensuremath{''}$ ($\sim$2400 AU) at a 10% level (Wilner & Welch 1994)

sensitivity.value: ~0.15 mJy/beam continuum; ~8 mJy/beam per channel lines

evidence.quote: The rms noise levels are $\sim$0.15 mJy beam $^{-1}$ in the 1.3 mm continuum image and $\sim$8 mJy beam$^{-1}$ per channel in the line images.
L1489 IRS was observed for 74 minutes (on-source time).
at the cycle 0 stage on 2012 August 9.

method.value: Point source plus Gaussian fit in image plane

analysis_steps.goal: Fit thin Keplerian disk to high-velocity C18O

method.value: chi2 fitting of axisymmetric geometrically-thin LTE disk model to convolved channel maps, staged free parameters

evidence.quote: we have built axisymmetric disk models with the geometrically-thin approximation, generated model C$^{18}$O images, and performed $\chi^2$ fitting to the observed channel maps of the high-velocity ($|V| \gtrsim 2.5$ km s$^{-1}$) C$^{18}$O emission.

key_parameters.value: Fit region central 2''x2'', velocities -6.1 to -2.5 and 2.5 to 7.1 km/s; Rd fixed 200 AU

evidence.quote: We select the central 2$\ensuremath{''}$ $\times$ 2$\ensuremath{''}$ region and the velocity ranges of $-$6.1 to $-$2.5 and 2.5 to 7.1 km s$^{-1}$

assumptions.value: d=140 pc, LTE, X(C18O)=3e-7, Gaussian line profile

evidence.quote: $d$ is the distance of 140 pc

fitting.value: Grid chi2 minimization with staged parameter sets; uncertainty from delta reduced chi2 = 1 with others fixed

evidence.quote: we adopt the parameter range that gives a reduced $\chi^2$ of 1+$\chi^2_{\rm min}$ as the fitting uncertainty

validation.value: Tested different initial p and q; residuals mostly <=3 sigma

evidence.quote: The levels of of residuals are all $\lesssim$4$\sigma$ and mostly $\lesssim$3$\sigma$

method.value: Optically thin dust mass M=F d^2/(kappa B(T))

evidence.quote: The mass of the Keplerian disk is then estimated to be $\sim$0.003–0.007 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ with a dust temperature of 55–25 K

evidence.quote: the mass opacity at 1.3 mm is 0.023 cm$^{2}$ g$^{-1}$ with $\beta = 1.0$

analysis_steps.goal: Flared disk and SO ring models

method.value: 3D flared disk (h0=25 AU, b=1.35) from best-fit; SO ring scaled C18O cube by SO/C18O ratio ~0.6 between 250-390 AU; compared via P-V diagrams

evidence.quote: we simply scaled the model C$^{18}$O image cubes by the SO/C$^{18}$O intensity ratio ($\sim$0.6) in the radial range of the ring
$T(r) = 44 \cdot (r/100\ {\rm AU})^{-0.3}$ K for simplicity

validation.value: Visual comparison of model and observed P-V diagrams

evidence.quote: The linear velocity gradient seen in the SO emission as well as the intensity peaks at positional offsets of $\sim$$\pm$2$\ensuremath{''}$ and velocities of $\sim$$\pm$2 km s$^{-1}$ can be reproduced with our ring model.

method.value: Trace protrusion ridges, fit parabolic Ulrich trajectories with Rc=300 AU and free theta0, phi0; build infall+disk model and compare moment maps and P-V with Keplerian-protrusion alternative

evidence.quote: we adopted the deprojected radius of these intensity peaks ($\sim$300 AU on the assumption the inclination angle of the disk plane $\sim$66$^\circ$) as the centrifugal radius of the infalling material

findings_qualitative.value: Off-axis C18O protrusions are distinct from the Keplerian disk and consistent with non-coplanar infalling flows

evidence.quote: One possibility of the nature of the non-Keplerian protrusions is that they trace infalling flows onto the Keplerian disk.

findings_qualitative.value: SO traces a ring in the flared disk, possibly accretion-shock enhanced at the centrifugal radius

evidence.quote: The local enhancement of the SO abundance in the ring region can be due to the accretion shocks at the centrifugal radius

claims.hypothesis: A Keplerian disk around L1489 IRS is traced by high-velocity CO/C18O
claims.experiment: chi2 fit of thin disk model to C18O channel maps
claims.result: M*=1.6 Msun, i=66 deg; disk radius up to ~700 AU
claims.finding: Keplerian disk with size and mass comparable to T Tauri disks

evidence.quote: The protostellar mass is estimated to be 1.6 $M_\ensuremath{\odot}$ with the inclination angle of 66$^\circ$.

claims.hypothesis: Off-axis C18O protrusions are infalling flows
claims.experiment: Parabolic trajectory models with conserved angular momentum compared with moment maps and P-V
claims.result: Infall model reproduces velocities better than coplanar Keplerian; rate ~5e-7 Msun/yr

evidence.quote: The shape and kinematics of these protrusions can be interpreted as streams of infalling flows with a conserved angular momentum following parabolic trajectories toward the Keplerian disk

claims.hypothesis: SO emission arises from a ring in the flared disk
claims.experiment: Ring model scaled from C18O flared disk model
claims.result: Reproduces linear velocity gradient for 250-390 AU
claims.finding: SO enhanced at accretion shock near centrifugal radius

evidence.quote: which is interpreted as that the SO emission primarily traces a ring region in the flared Keplerian disk at radii of $\sim$250–390 AU

why_this_data.value: Higher resolution and sensitivity than SMA to resolve transition from infalling envelope to disk

evidence.quote: providing an angular resolution four times better and sensitivity more than ten times better than those of the previous SMA observations

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Protrusions as outflow or optical depth effects or coplanar Keplerian rotation were disfavored

evidence.quote: these protrusions are unlikely to be related with the outflow, because the direction of the velocity gradient of the protrusions

limitations_admitted.value: Missing flux (~80% of C18O) hinders outer disk radius; p, q, T0, vturb poorly constrained

evidence.quote: it is difficult to unambiguously constrain the outer radius of the Keplerian disk due to the effect of the missing flux ($\sim$80%; Hogerheijde et al. 1998)
We found that $p$, $q$, $T_0$, and $v_{\rm turb}$ are not well constrained by our fitting.

Missing flux (~80%) and outflow contamination affect the medium/low-velocity C18O
